problem.text: Ted mistakenly wrote $2^m\cdot\sqrt{\frac{1}{4096}}$ as $2\cdot\sqrt[m]{\frac{1}{4096}}$. What is the sum of all real numbers $m$ for which these two expressions have the same value?

steps.title: Where to start: write everything as a power of 2
steps.body: Both expressions are built from $2$ and $4096$. When a problem mixes one base with roots, a good first move is to write every piece as a power of that base. Here $4096 = 2^{12}$, so $\frac{1}{4096} = 2^{-12}$.

your_turn.answer: $2^{-6}$, because a square root halves the exponent: $-12 \div 2 = -6$.

steps.title: Rewrite both sides
steps.body: The left side is $2^m \cdot 2^{-6} = 2^{m-6}$. An $m$-th root divides the exponent by $m$, so the right side is $2 \cdot 2^{-12/m} = 2^{1 - 12/m}$. Careful: do not lose the factor $2$ in front on the right side; it adds $1$ to the exponent.

your_turn.prompt: Why is it enough to set the two exponents equal?
your_turn.answer: Two powers of $2$ are equal only when their exponents are equal.

steps.title: Turn it into a quadratic
steps.body:
Setting the exponents equal gives the equation below. The value $m = 0$ is not allowed (there is no zeroth root), so you may multiply both sides by $m$.
$$m - 6 = 1 - \frac{12}{m}$$

your_turn.prompt: Multiply both sides by $m$ and move everything to one side. What equation do you get?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The quadratic factors as $(m-3)(m-4) = 0$, so $m = 3$ or $m = 4$. Both are nonzero real numbers, and both work: for $m=3$ each side is $2^{-3}$, and for $m=4$ each side is $2^{-2}$. The sum is $3 + 4 = 7$. The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.B: This comes from dropping the factor $2$ on the right side, which gives $m - 6 = -\frac{12}{m}$, or $m^2 - 6m + 12 = 0$, whose roots would sum to $6$. But that quadratic has no real roots (its discriminant is $36 - 48 < 0$), which is a sign the setup went wrong.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
